==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:soule|id=spirit|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|soule}}, {{m|enm|sowle}}, {{m|enm|saule}}, {{m|enm|sawle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sāwol|t=soul, life, spirit, being}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*saiwalu}}, from  {{inh|en|gem-pro|*saiwalō|t=soul}}, of an uncertain ultimate origin (see there for further information). 
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|saul}}, {{m|sco|sowel|t=soul}}, {{cog|stq|Seele|t=soul}}, {{cog|fy|siel|t=soul}}, {{cog|gsw|Seel|t=soul}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Siel|t=soul}}, {{cog|nl|ziel|t=soul}}, {{cog|de|Seele|t=soul}}, {{cog|nds-de|Seel|t=soul}}, {{cog|lb|Séil|t=soul, spirit}}, {{cog|wym|zejł}}, {{m|wym|zəjł}}, {{m|wym|zyił|t=soul}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌰𐌹𐍅𐌰𐌻𐌰|t=soul}}. Scandinavian homonyms seem to have been borrowed from {{cog|osx|sēola}}. Modern {{cog|da|sjæl|t=soul}}, {{cog|is|sál|t=soul}}, {{cog|nb|sjel|t=soul}}, {{cog|nn|sjel}}, {{m|nn|sål|t=soul}}, {{cog|sv|själ|t=soul}}, {{cog|fi|sielu|t=soul}} may have come from {{cog|ang|sāwol}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|religion|folklore}} The [[spirit]] or [[essence]] of a person usually thought to consist of one's thoughts and personality, often believed to live on after the person's death.
#* '''1836''', {{w|Hans Christian Andersen}} (translated into English by Mrs. H. B. Paull in 1872), {{w|The Little Mermaid}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=46|passage=No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or{{...}}. And at last I began to realize in my harassed '''soul''' that all elusion was futile, and to take such holidays as I could get, when he was off with a girl, in a spirit of thankfulness.}}
#* {{RQ:Undertale|passage= Flowey: See that heart? That is your '''SOUL''', the very culmination of your being!}}
# The spirit or essence of anything.
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=From another point of view, it was a place without a '''soul'''. The well-to-do had hearts of stone; the rich were brutally bumptious; the Press, the Municipality, all the public men, were ridiculously, vaingloriously self-satisfied.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1928
|author=w:Franklin D. Roosevelt
|title=The Happy Warrior Alfred E. Smith
|url=https://archive.org/details/happywarrioralfr006717mbp/
|publisher=w:Houghton Mifflin
|OCLC=769015
|OL=6719278M
|pages=36–37
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/happywarrioralfr006717mbp/page/n48/
|text=It is possible with only these qualities for a man to be a reasonably efficient President, but there is one thing more needed to make him a great President. It is that quality of '''soul''' which makes a man loved by little children, by dumb animals, that quality of '''soul''' which makes him a strong help to all those in sorrow or in trouble, that quality which makes him not merely admired, but loved by all the people - the quality of sympathetic understanding of the human heart, of real interest in one's fellow men.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:Architectural Digest|date=May 2026|volume=83|issue=4|title=The Rest is History|author=Julie Coe|quotee=Annie Monnier|page=36
|text="There's a vibrancy that comes from the building's historic '''soul''' metting the rhythm of the Caribbean," says Monnier.}}
# [[life|Life]], [[energy]], [[vigor]].
#* {{RQ:Young Love of Fame|page=52|passage=That he vvants Algebra he muſt confeſs. / ''But not a '''ſoul''' to give our arms ſucceſs.''}}
# Cultural consciousness and pride among people of African American heritage.<ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online|entry=soul|cultural consciousness and pride among people of African heritage}}</ref>
# A strong positive feeling of intense sensitivity and emotional fervor conveyed especially by African American performers.<ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online|entry=soul|passage=a strong positive feeling (as of intense sensitivity and emotional fervor) conveyed especially by African American performers}}</ref>
# {{lb|en|music}} [[soul music|Soul music]].
# A [[person]], especially as one among [[many]].
#* '''18 January 1915''', {{w|D. H. Lawrence}}, ''letter to William Hopkin''
#*: I want to gather together about twenty '''souls''' and sail away from this world of war and squalor and found a little colony where there shall be no money but a sort of communism as far as necessaries of life go, and some real decency.
# An individual life.
#: {{ux|en|Fifty '''souls''' were lost when the ship sank.}}
# {{lb|en|math}} A kind of [[submanifold]] involved in the {{w|soul theorem}} of [[Riemannian geometry]].
